summary: Okanogan County, WA summit lookout near the Pasayten Wilderness; 1934 L-4 lookout burned accidentally in 1957 and was never replaced. Captioned footings mark a hike-in summit.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a short tower (10 ft or 15 ft per sources); earlier log and frame cupola cabin from the 1920s
facts.status_note: Burned in 1957 and never replaced; sources describe footings, an anchor and rock work at the summit

access.note: Reached on hiking trail only; no closure for this trail is listed on the Forest Service page read

visit.trail_note: Forest Service Trail 538 from Billy Goat Trailhead via Billy Goat Pass; final 0.6 mile climbs a steep talus slope; unmarked side trail to the summit; not officially maintained for many years and not for stock use

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest today)

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: the register and Firelookout.com say 10 ft, WillhiteWeb says 15 ft. The record's 4.3 m (about 14 ft) matches neither, so facts.height_m is left out; a human should check where the record's figure came from. The 1931 'Birch Mountain' item is filed under Burch by Forest Lookouts, but the paper's spelling differs and the match is unconfirmed. Built 1934 and burned 1957 agree across all sources. Today's condition comes from undated WillhiteWeb captions only. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads.
